# Potentially Suspicious PowerShell Child Processes

Last updated on:

In this page

 About the rule
 Rule Requirement
 Detection

## About the rule

### Rule Type

### Rule Description

Detects potentially suspicious child processes spawned by PowerShell. Use this rule to hunt for potential anomalies initiating from PowerShell scripts and commands.

### Severity

## Rule Requirement

### Criteria [...] `Action1: actionname = "Process started" AND (PARENTPROCESSNAME endswith "\powershell_ise.exe,\powershell.exe,\pwsh.exe" AND PROCESSNAME endswith "\bash.exe,\bitsadmin.exe,\certutil.exe,\cscript.exe,\forfiles.exe,\hh.exe,\mshta.exe,\regsvr32.exe,\rundll32.exe,\schtasks.exe,\scrcons.exe,\scriptrunner.exe,\sh.exe,\wmic.exe,\wscript.exe") AND ((PROCESSNAME notendswith "\certutil.exe" OR COMMANDLINE notcontains "-verifystore ") AND (PROCESSNAME notendswith "\wmic.exe" OR COMMANDLINE notcontains

Detects suspicious child processes related to Windows Shell utilities spawned by `conhost.exe`, which could indicate malicious activity using trusted system components.
